newsitem.title: POLAND: BankAmerica eyes Polish branch, equity.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica eyes Polish branch, equity.

text.p: California-based BankAmerica, which applied last week to open a subsidiary in Warsaw, plans equity investment in Poland that could reach tens of millions of dollars over the next few years, bank officials said.
"Our...major initiative is to expand the activity of the bank and open a subsidiary in Poland," Daniel Wood, the bank's country manager in Poland, told a news conference on Thursday.
He said the bank wanted to provide capital investment financing and corporate banking services to mulitinationals, Polish firms, joint ventures, and government and municipal agencies.
The targeted sectors were mostly telecommunications, energy, power and oil and gas industries.
Wood also said the bank would invest in Polish companies through its Warsaw representative office, which opened in June.
"Unique in the Polish market is that Bank of America through the representative office will be investing in the equity of Polish companies," Wood said.
BankAmerica officials declined to give an exact amount or time frame for the planned investment but said the number could approach $50 million over a few years.

They said the investments would be five-to-15-percent venture capital investments in mid-sized Polish companies before they were listed on the Warsaw bourse, where they could be floated after a number of years if the firms prospered.
"We don't take management control, that's up to the local entrepreneur," said Ralph Schauss, Group Executive for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
Poland is the bank's first representative office to open in the region since the Moscow office started in 1976.
"Bank of America has its origins in California, which has had a very high growth period over the last few years -- basically we see the same sort of environment here in Poland today," Wood said.
